items.title: ‘Human’ wins Cambridge dictionary’s word of the year

items.title: Can Labour end the youth unemployment crisis? – podcast

items.title: Milburn’s absurdly ambitious report offers blueprint for fixing everything and everyone
items.desc: He lays out sweeping aims and finer details for how to fix the Neets crisis – and is obsessive about welfare Neet ideas: what’s in Milburn’s report? It is not clear if too many people were expecting Everything Everywhere All at Once, but that is what Alan Milburn has delivered. From a Welfare State to a Working State is almost absurdly ambitious. The terms of reference said something about the drivers of youth labour markets. We got a blueprint for how to fix everything and everyone. What Keir Starmer, who commissioned it, had in mind, we’ll never know, but Milburn has taken up with gusto Andy Burnham’s general invocation to think boldly and rewire the state. Yes, it’s about training and jobs, but it’s also about pulling apart the NHS, giving schools and colleges an MOT, and once again, blowing up old-fashioned social security . Continue reading...
